note: PROVENANCE, rewritten 2026-09-24. The FIELD SHAPE of every dataset row below was taken from real runs of these four actors from this account on 2026-09-24 - the run ids are in docs/RESEARCH-PACK-PILOT-2026-09-24.md - and the identifiers were then replaced with reserved-domain and invented equivalents, because tests/test_fixture_hygiene.py refuses a real company or person in a tracked file and is right to. So the shape is a capture and the content is not, which is the only combination this repository allows. What this file replaced was neither: it was written to three actor ids that answer 404 record-not-found, so nothing it asserted could ever have run.
The pack runs the website crawler too - the fourth source. This entry must sort BEFORE apify.json's own crawler entry, which is what the 00- prefix is for.

One SUCCEEDED per run id, each naming ITS OWN dataset. A generic status reply made the run fall through to apify.json's catch-all `/datasets/` entry and read another actor's rows - which is what a shared match does when the ids do not discriminate.

THE FIRST ROW IS A DIFFERENT COMPANY. `companyName` is a text filter, so a search for one name returns another company's jobs, and that row's `companyUrl` is another company's LinkedIn page. `actors.slug_from_jobs` must walk past it and take the slug from the row whose `companyWebsite` is on the record's own domain. Without this row the slug test passes on a list of one and proves nothing.
